tickets_per_week.text: How many tickets a week go through this path?

chained_by_hand.text: Are the phases chained by hand today?

values.no: something already starts the next phase

symptoms.text: What did you measure on your own runs?

ticket_workflow.label: a ticket workflow for a team, driving a coding agent

own_agent_app.label: your own agent application in Python or TypeScript, with a known graph and pauses in the process
own_agent_app.choice: LangGraph, or an agent SDK plus an engine
own_agent_app.why: You write the agent application yourself, the graph is known, and a run must pause inside the process.
own_agent_app.would_change: The number of runs that must pause for a person inside the process. At zero, or when the flow is a straight line, a script is enough; when the step already runs inside a coding agent, use skills and hooks.

agent_product.label: an agent product for users, with sessions that resume mid-run
agent_product.choice: A durable engine under a plain loop
agent_product.why: Sessions of your users must resume mid-run. That is where Cursor and Replit use an engine.
agent_product.would_change: The number of sessions that must resume mid-run. At zero, this row of the table no longer describes you: answer again.

many_repositories.label: the same change across hundreds of repositories
many_repositories.choice: A script and a CI matrix, one PR per repository
many_repositories.why: It is a different job from one ticket to one pull request: a script fans out, with one writer per repository.
many_repositories.would_change: The number of repositories that get the change. The report says "hundreds" in its table and "tens or hundreds of independent units" in its grid: it gives no lower bound. For "several" repositories its grid names something else, a versioned plugin and a reusable CI workflow.
many_repositories.source: report §8, fifth row; report §7, questions 5 and 7

long_lived_orchestrator.label: a long-lived orchestrator, a tool server or a binary for many teams
long_lived_orchestrator.why: The code part is a program worth compiling: a binary handed to many repositories, or an orchestrator that lives long. Rust buys nothing on the duration or the model cost of a ticket.
long_lived_orchestrator.would_change: The number of teams or repositories the binary is handed to. For one team whose runners have Python, standard-library Python is the cheapest to change.

symptoms.symptom: Runs die far in and pay their tokens twice
symptoms.counts: the share of runs that died far in and were paid twice, from 0 to 1
symptoms.written: more than about one run in ten
symptoms.smallest_fix: Shorter jobs; progress written on the pull request between jobs

symptoms.counts: the number of tickets that had two runs at once
symptoms.smallest_fix: One run at a time per ticket; keys derived from the ticket, never random
symptoms.removed_by: An engine with one workflow per ticket

symptoms.symptom: An event accepted, nothing happened, nobody told
symptoms.counts: the number of events that were accepted and then lost without a word
symptoms.smallest_fix: A job timeout; a scheduled sweep; a final status written by code

symptoms.symptom: An agent loops and burns tokens
symptoms.counts: the number of runs where the agent looped until something outside stopped it
symptoms.smallest_fix: A budget cap per run; empty turns count as failure
symptoms.removed_by: Nothing. An engine retries it faithfully

symptoms.symptom: A wait that must resume inside an expensive multi-step computation
symptoms.counts: the number of waits that must resume inside an expensive multi-step computation
symptoms.smallest_fix: Model the wait as a ticket state

symptoms.symptom: Many steps, each with its own retry and timeout rule
symptoms.counts: the number of steps that need a retry or timeout rule of their own
symptoms.left_to_you: The report says "many steps" and gives no number, so this command names no threshold: whether {value} is many is yours to judge
symptoms.removed_by: An engine; count one to two days per workflow

symptoms.symptom: Strict order across events from several systems
symptoms.counts: the number of events from several systems that were handled out of order
symptoms.removed_by: An engine, or a database constraint

symptoms.symptom: You cannot say what a ticket cost
symptoms.counts: the number of tickets whose cost nobody can give
symptoms.smallest_fix: The step writes tokens and dollars on the pull request
symptoms.removed_by: Any runtime with a run record

by_hand.sentence: By hand with the ai-sdlc skills may be enough: no ticket goes through this path yet.
by_hand.why: No ticket goes through this path in a week and the phases are chained by hand: there is nothing to chain yet. The ai-sdlc skills, run one after the other by a person, can do the work.
by_hand.would_change: tickets_per_week above 0. Zero is this command's own rule: neither the guide nor the report gives a number of tickets a week under which by hand is enough.
by_hand.source: decide.md §7 ("Chaining the steps by hand may be enough")

ticket_state_and_ci.sentence: Ticket state and CI are enough.
ticket_state_and_ci.why_by_hand: {tickets} tickets a week go through this path and the phases are chained by hand. The ticket or the pull request holds the state, and a short CI job runs each step. No measured symptom is above its threshold.
ticket_state_and_ci.why_chained: The phases are already chained without a person, and no measured symptom is above its threshold. The ticket or the pull request holds the state, and a short CI job runs each step.
ticket_state_and_ci.would_change: One symptom measured above its threshold on your own runs: runs_paid_twice above 0.1, any other above 0, except steps_with_own_retry_rule, which has no threshold and is yours to judge.
ticket_state_and_ci.source: report §8, first row; report §7, last table

symptom.why: On a ticket workflow, a measured symptom is the only thing that calls for more than ticket state and CI. Try the smallest fix first; move on only when the symptom is still there.
symptom.would_change: Each symptom named above back at or under its threshold after its smallest fix: then ticket state and CI are enough.
symptom.engine: If one stays, the report's choice is a managed engine (Temporal Cloud), one workflow per ticket; the worker can be Rust.
symptom.source: report §7, last table; report §8, second row; decide.md §3
